messages:
anna: Heads-up: sales asked for a lightweight "ephemeral pin" flow so customers can test model variants during migrations without a full onboarding. want a quick spec.
paul: What does "ephemeral" mean here? TTL? scope?
anna: TTL = 30 days max, customer-scoped, visible in catalog but marked ephemeral. routing preference only, not a hard commit.
devops: Implementation: routing tag + customer priority flag. estimate 3 dev-days + 1 QA day. no infra reprovisioning.
paul: Acceptance tests (minimal): 1) perf smoke (95p latency), 2) top-10 regression prompts, 3) audit log entry on create/delete. keep it small.
legal: require immutable audit trail exportable on request; ephemeral pins must not imply SLA. include liability disclaimer.
salesbot: Messaging: offer a "migration credit" if customer converts to permanent pin within 14 days of expiry. need billing hook.
anna: UX: catalog needs ephemeral badge, start/end date, one-click convert-to-permanent. small mock needed (2-3 pts).
devops: Canary plan: internal -> 5% traffic -> 20% over 48h windows. auto-failback if regression > threshold.
paul: Backlog items: ep-pin-routing, ep-pin-ui-badge, ep-pin-audit-export, billing-credit-hook, ep-pin-canary-runbook. Prioritize routing + audit + UI for pilot.
anna: Pilot with two customers next sprint. owners: devops -> routing, paul -> harness + criteria, salesbot -> billing + comms, legal -> template. Reconvene Thu after infra PR.
legal: Template ready by Fri; will make sure wording disclaims SLA for ephemeral.
anna: Good. I'll add to roadmap doc and create tickets.
salesbot: I'll prep customer comms and pilot invites.
anna: Thanks. Short, pragmatic scope to get wins without promising infra SLAs
